heading: Merchant Deposit Agreement
memo_rationale: The fee-addition mechanism defeats the cap. The bank reliance, ownership, release, and hold-harmless language reaches funds and conduct beyond Buyer’s percentage and cannot establish a nonsignatory bank’s duties. Require aligned forms and preserve responsibility for wrongful instructions.
memo_replacement: Merchant shall provide the information and processor authorizations reasonably necessary to verify and remit Purchased Receipts. Every amount deducted from the Purchase Price must appear as a separate dollar item in Section 1.4 before Merchant signs and must be lawfully disclosed. Buyer may not collect an undisclosed or unearned deduction. No fee is added to the Purchased Amount or Remaining Balance or collected through the split. Any separate lawful enforcement expense is governed solely by Section 6.3. Buyer owns only Purchased Receipts and identifiable proceeds of that purchased share. This Agreement neither changes a bank’s duties nor releases any person from liability for unauthorized instructions, negligence, fraud, or violation of law. Buyer is responsible for the accuracy and scope of instructions it or its agents issue. Collection authorizations terminate as provided in Section 2.6.
current_body:
Merchant shall execute an agreement (the “Merchant Deposit Agreement”) acceptable to Buyer and have the Approved Bank Account with a depository institution (“Bank”) acceptable to Buyer. Merchant shall provide Buyer and/or its authorized agent with the information and authorizations necessary to verify Merchant’s Receipts into the Approved Bank Account.
Merchant authorizes its merchant processor and applicable third parties to provide Buyer all information necessary to permit Buyer to determine the Specified Percentage due.
Buyer may charge fees as set forth on Appendix A (the “Fee Structure”); such fees are added to the Remaining Balance and collected through the same settlement remittance as the Purchased Amount. Every amount deducted from the Purchase Price before delivery to Merchant must appear as a line in the itemization in Section 1.4 and be stated as a dollar figure before Merchant signs. Buyer may not deduct any amount that does not so appear.
The foregoing authorizations shall continue in effect until Buyer receives final payment of the entire Purchased Amount and all other amounts due. Bank may rely upon the instructions of Buyer without independent verification. Merchant waives any claim for damages against Bank in connection with actions taken based upon instructions from Buyer, unless such damages were due to Bank’s failure to follow Buyer’s instructions.
Merchant acknowledges that: (i) Bank will be acting on behalf of Buyer with respect to portions of the Purchased Amount until remitted to Buyer through the settlement process; (ii) Bank may or may not be an affiliate of Buyer; (iii) Merchant has no power or authority to control Bank’s or Buyer’s actions with respect to remittance; (iv) Buyer is not responsible and shall not be liable for the actions of Bank, and Merchant agrees to hold Buyer harmless; and (v) funds representing the Purchased Amount in the possession of Bank and Buyer constitute property owned solely by Buyer, and Merchant disclaims any and all interest therein.
my_note: Adopt the fee-addition fix (it is 013 again). Push back on one point: the memo would have us preserve responsibility for wrongful instructions, which is right, but the bank reliance and hold-harmless language should be deleted rather than narrowed — we cannot establish a non-signatory bank's duties by contract with the merchant, so narrowing it just leaves an unenforceable clause that reads as if it works.

heading: Right to Cancel
memo_rationale: The draft is unclear whether Net Amount Funded includes third-party payoffs, and it does not specify how withheld fees are reversed. The prior note’s assumption that the merchant necessarily loses every fee is not established by the definition supplied. The replacement makes the unwind explicit and usable, including an old-balance payoff that cannot be reversed.
memo_replacement:
Merchant may cancel by sending notice under Section 7.3 no later than the third calendar day after the Purchase Date. If that day is not a Workday, the deadline extends to the next Workday. Within three Workdays after timely notice, Merchant shall return the cash actually received plus amounts actually paid to third parties at Merchant’s written direction that Buyer has not recovered, less collections Buyer already received under this Agreement. Any Buyer fee withheld at funding is cancelled and is not included in that return amount; a Buyer fee separately paid by Merchant is credited against the return amount or refunded once. No unearned purchase discount is payable. Buyer shall stop withholding promptly and provide an itemized unwind statement.
For a prior transaction owed to Buyer and settled internally from this purchase, cancellation reverses that settlement and restores only the prior contractual purchase rights and Remaining Balance existing immediately before settlement, adjusted for all intervening collections, without a new fee, increase, or maturity; the internal payoff is not also included in the return amount. Merchant may instead elect to keep that prior purchase extinguished and include its actual agreed settlement amount in the return amount. Any restoration is subject to applicable law and does not automatically revive a released lien or its former priority. Third-party payoffs that cannot be recovered remain in the return calculation and must be specifically highlighted before acceptance. No amount is counted twice. Separate equipment return rights are governed by the equipment agreement. Any more favorable mandatory cancellation right controls.
current_body: Merchant has the right to cancel this Agreement within three (3) calendar days after Buyer has delivered the Net Amount Funded. Merchant may exercise this right by notifying Buyer in writing that it is cancelling this Agreement and returning the Net Amount Funded to Buyer, including any payoffs made on Merchant’s behalf by Buyer. For the cancellation to be effective, Buyer must receive both the notice and the return of the funds within three (3) calendar days after Buyer has delivered the Net Amount Funded.
my_note: Adopt the explicit unwind. The memo correctly notes our prior assumption — that the merchant necessarily forfeits every fee — is not established by the definition supplied. Make the withheld-fee reversal explicit rather than assuming either answer.

heading: Voluntary Prepayment
memo_rationale: “Without penalty” does not tell Merchant whether early delivery saves any discount or finance charge. Use early-completion terminology, disclose the actual full-face economics, and preserve mandatory rebates. A discount is not universally required merely because collection occurs early.
memo_replacement: Merchant may voluntarily deliver all or part of the remaining Purchased Amount early without an additional early-completion fee. Unless Section 1 expressly provides a discount or applicable law requires a rebate, early completion requires the full Remaining Balance and does not reduce the original agreed purchase discount. Buyer shall state that result clearly in the offer and applicable disclosures. On request, Buyer shall promptly provide a dated written settlement quote showing credits, any discount or rebate, and the exact amount that ends collection. Early completion is optional, not an obligation on a scheduled date, and Buyer shall comply with Section 2.6 after receiving the agreed completion amount.
current_body: Merchant may, at any time and without penalty, deliver to Buyer any or all of the unpaid Purchased Amount before its full collection in the ordinary course. Voluntary prepayment shall not relieve Merchant of any obligation accrued prior to the prepayment date, but shall extinguish all future remittance obligations under this Agreement upon receipt of the full Purchased Amount.
my_note: 'Without penalty' tells a merchant nothing about whether early completion saves any money. Use early-completion terminology and disclose the actual full-face economics.

memo_rationale: Adding all fees to Remaining Balance extends the purchased pool and permits disputed charges to be swept. The actual fee table/rates are not supplied. Use a closed, fully itemized schedule and prohibit a generic discretionary fee power.
memo_replacement: Only fees expressly identified by type, dollar amount or lawful calculation method, payee, purpose, and collection timing in the completed Appendix A and required disclosures before acceptance may be charged. A blank or omitted fee is $0.00. No fee is added to the Purchased Amount or Remaining Balance or collected through the processor split. No fee is charged solely for reconciliation, receipts decline, ordinary business failure, data-access interruption, or exercising a legal right. Enforcement expenses are governed exclusively by Section 6.3. A waived fee is irrevocably removed from amounts claimed, while its audit record may be retained.
current_body: All fees are added to the Remaining Balance and are collectible via the same methods as the Purchased Amount. Fees may be voided by Buyer in its discretion, but voided fees remain on record for audit purposes.
my_note: Critical and it is 013 again at the fee schedule. Adding all fees to Remaining Balance extends the purchased pool and lets a disputed charge be swept out of settlements before anyone adjudicates it. A closed, itemised schedule with no generic discretionary fee power. The actual rates were never supplied — get them.

memo_rationale: “Not charging ISO fees” can mislead when the merchant’s origination charge funds the commission. Disclose total merchant cost and payor plainly without pretending every commission must be a separate merchant fee.
memo_replacement: The Origination Fee, if any, is the dollar amount itemized in Section 1.4 and Appendix A. Buyer shall identify the portion paid to an ISO or broker and make any compensation disclosure required by law. That commission is included in the disclosed transaction cost and does not authorize an additional direct ISO charge to Merchant. No statement that there is “no ISO fee” may conceal the source or amount of Merchant’s total charges. Unauthorized charges are addressed under Section 7.21.
current_body: Some or all of the Origination Fee may be paid to an independent sales organization (“ISO”). Otherwise, Buyer is NOT charging any ISO fees to Merchant. If Merchant is charged another such fee, Merchant acknowledges that it is not being charged by Buyer.
my_note: 'We do not charge ISO fees' is misleading when the merchant's origination charge funds the commission. Disclose total merchant cost and who is paid.

memo_rationale: The existing actual/reasonable and aggregate-cap language is sound in principle. Remove parallel operative wording so adjudication, guarantor limits, and no-sweep treatment are identical everywhere.
memo_replacement: Attorneys’ fees, court costs, collection expenses, and any statutory interest are recoverable only under Section 6.3, including its proof, adjudication or settlement, aggregate-cap, no-duplication, and limited-guaranty requirements. They are not calculated or earned automatically as a percentage of the uncollected Purchased Amount.
current_body: Attorneys’ Fees / Collection Fees: Buyer may recover its attorneys’ fees and collection fees actually incurred and reasonable in amount. These are not calculated as a percentage of the undelivered Purchased Amount, and together with every other enforcement cost recoverable under this Agreement they are subject to the aggregate limit in Section 6.3.
my_note: Align the wording with 055 so the adjudication requirement, guarantor limits and no-sweep treatment read identically in both places.
